topics.name: Conjunctions (and, but, or, because, if, that, when, although)
Instructions with modals: should, must, may, have to, ought to

options: Riya practises yoga because of she wants to stay fit.
Riya practises yoga because she wants to stay fit.
Riya practises yoga because she want to stay fit.
questions.rule: because joins a full clause (subject + verb): because she wants. because of needs a noun.

options: Ouch! I has twisted my ankle.
Ouch! I have twist my ankle.
Ouch! I have twisted my ankle.
questions.rule: Ouch! shows pain. With I, use have + past participle: I have twisted.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: learn
learning
learnt

questions.rule: After a modal like should, use the base verb: should learn.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: coming
came
come

questions.rule: A negative instruction is Do not + base verb: Do not come up.

questions.before: I wanted to join the yoga class,
options: because
so
but
questions.rule: but joins two ideas that contrast: I wanted to join, but it was full.

questions.after: We have won the yoga contest!
options: Hurrah!
Ouch!
Alas!
questions.rule: Hurrah! shows joy. Ouch! shows pain and Alas! shows sadness.
An instruction begins with the base verb: Lie face down on the mat.

questions.prompt: Make a rule for yoga practice.
questions.rule: Negative modal: must not + base verb: You must not eat.

chat: How do I start the cobra pose?
options: First, lying face down and relax completely.
First, lie face down and relaxing completely.
First, lie face down and relax completely.
questions.rule: Instructions use the base verb, and and joins two of them: lie ... and relax.

questions.source: It is a very nice picture.
options: What a nice picture it is!
What nice picture it is!
How a nice picture it is!
questions.rule: Use What a + adjective + noun for a singular noun: What a nice picture it is!

options: You may to practise outdoors on level ground.
You may practise outdoors on level ground.
You may practising outdoors on level ground.
questions.rule: may (permission) is followed by the base verb without to: may practise.

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct passive verb.
options: Asanas are practised in a clean, airy room.
Asanas are practise in a clean, airy room.
Asanas is practised in a clean, airy room.
questions.rule: Passive = is/are + past participle. Plural asanas takes are practised.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: practising
practises
practised

questions.rule: Passive voice needs the past participle after is: is practised.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: slower
slowly
slowness

questions.rule: To tell how you raise your head, use the adverb slowly.

options: smooth
smoothly
smoothness
questions.rule: The word tells how to come down, so use the adverb smoothly.

options: loves
is loved
is love
questions.rule: by many beginners shows a passive sentence: is + past participle = is loved.

questions.prompt: Join the ideas in one sentence.
questions.rule: but joins two contrasting clauses. A comma usually comes before it.

chat: I got full marks in the science test!
options: Wow! That's a wonderful news.
Wow! That wonderful news is.
Wow! That's wonderful news.
questions.rule: Wow! shows surprise and joy. News is uncountable, so no a.

chat: Can I practise yoga right after lunch?
options: No, you should wait for a few hours after a meal.
No, you should waiting for a few hours after a meal.
No, you should to wait for a few hours after a meal.
questions.rule: should (advice) is followed by the base verb: should wait.

options: The steps were explained by the teacher.
The steps are explain by the teacher.
The steps are explained by the teacher.
questions.rule: Simple present active becomes are + past participle: The steps are explained.

options: Both Sahil and Rohan enjoys the eagle pose.
Both Sahil or Rohan enjoy the eagle pose.
Both Sahil and Rohan enjoy the eagle pose.
questions.rule: Both ... and go together, and two people take a plural verb: enjoy.

options: Does he have to bring his own mat?
Does he has to bring his own mat?
Do he have to bring his own mat?
questions.rule: Question with have to: Does he have to ...? After does, use the base form have.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: named
naming
names

questions.rule: Passive voice: was + past participle: was named after.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: or
but
so

questions.rule: The pair is not only ... but also.

questions.after: you are a beginner, you should learn from a teacher.
options: So
If
And
questions.rule: If introduces a condition: If you are a beginner, you should ...

questions.after: not inhale immediately after the lion pose.
options: have
should
are
questions.rule: should not + base verb gives advice. have not inhale and are not inhale are wrong.
The adverb upwards comes after the object your spine; as you exhale tells when.

chat: When is International Yoga Day celebrated?
options: It celebrated on 21st June every year.
It is celebrate on 21st June every year.
It is celebrated on 21st June every year.
questions.rule: The question is passive, so answer in the passive: It is celebrated.

questions.source: Meera did not come to school. She was ill.
options: Meera did not came to school because she was ill.
Meera did not come to school because she is ill.
Meera did not come to school because she was ill.
questions.rule: because gives the reason. Keep both verbs in the past: did not come, was ill.

questions.source: You must hold your breath for a long time.
options: You must not to hold your breath for a long time.
You must not hold your breath for a long time.
You do not must hold your breath for a long time.
questions.rule: Put not after the modal: must not hold.

options: Ravi has felt fitter since he joined the yoga class.
Ravi felt fitter since he has joined the yoga class.
Ravi has felt fitter since he has join the yoga class.
questions.rule: Main clause in present perfect (has felt), and since + simple past (joined).

options: Garudasana, which is named after the eagle, improves balance.
Garudasana, who is named after the eagle, improves balance.
Garudasana, which is named after the eagle, improve balance.
questions.rule: Use which for things, is named for the passive, and singular improves.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: practising
practise
practised

questions.rule: ought to is followed by the base verb: ought to practise.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: steadily
steadier
steadiness

questions.rule: To compare how two people balance, use more + adverb: more steadily.

options: perfected
is perfecting
was perfected
questions.rule: Yoga did not do the perfecting; people did. So use the past passive: was perfected.
that joins the message to the verb tell: Tell him that ...

chat: Ouch! I have hurt my knee.
options: Oh no! Sits down and rest for a while.
Oh no! Sit down and resting for a while.
Oh no! Sit down and rest for a while.
questions.rule: After the interjection Oh no!, give advice with base verbs: Sit down and rest.

chat: Do you have to go to the yoga camp tomorrow?
options: Yes, I have to been there by six o'clock.
Yes, I has to be there by six o'clock.
Yes, I have to be there by six o'clock.
questions.rule: I have to + base verb: I have to be there.

questions.source: The poses are shown by Sameer.
options: Sameer shows the poses.
Sameer showed the poses.
Sameer is shown the poses.
questions.rule: Present passive are shown becomes simple present active: Sameer shows the poses.

questions.source: You are at home. You should help your parents.
options: When you are at home, you should helps your parents.
When you at home, you should help your parents.
When you are at home, you should help your parents.
questions.rule: When + a full clause (you are at home), then a comma and the main clause.

options: Although the pose looks simple, but it must be learnt from an instructor.
Although the pose looks simple, it must be learnt from an instructor.
Although the pose looks simple, it must be learn from an instructor.
questions.rule: Do not use but after although. Passive with a modal: must be learnt.

options: Wow! How graceful you balanced in the eagle pose!
Wow! How gracefully you balanced in the eagle pose!
Wow! How gracefully did you balanced in the eagle pose!
questions.rule: gracefully tells how you balanced, and an exclamation keeps statement order: How gracefully you balanced!

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: included
including
includes

questions.rule: Passive with a modal: should be + past participle: should be included.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: gently
gentler
gentleness

questions.rule: The word tells how you come back, so use the adverb gently.

questions.after: it is very good for the face and throat muscles.
options: so
yet
because
questions.rule: yet (like but) joins two ideas that contrast: it looks funny, yet it is useful.
Passive with a modal: must be + past participle: must be learnt.

chat: Why did you join the yoga class?
options: I joined it because of my back felt stiff after long hours of study.
I joined it because my back feel stiff after long hours of study.
I joined it because my back felt stiff after long hours of study.
questions.rule: because + clause in the past: because my back felt stiff.

chat: I can't touch my toes yet. Should I push harder?
options: No, you shouldn't forcing it. Your body will slowly become more flexible.
No, you shouldn't force it. Your body will slowly becomes more flexible.
No, you shouldn't force it. Your body will slowly become more flexible.
questions.rule: Modals shouldn't and will are followed by the base verb: force, become.

questions.source: People all over the world celebrate International Yoga Day.
options: International Yoga Day was celebrated by people all over the world.
International Yoga Day is celebrated by people all over the world.
International Yoga Day is celebrating by people all over the world.
questions.rule: Simple present active becomes is + past participle: is celebrated.

questions.source: How flexible the yoga teacher is!
options: The yoga teacher is very flexibly.
The yoga teacher is very flexible.
The yoga teacher are very flexible.
questions.rule: Replace How with very, use statement order and a full stop: The yoga teacher is very flexible.
